g_roast: I've seen tidier scrums in the under nines, boys, and half of them were crying for their mams.
Look at this lot, honest to God, if you were scaffolding I'd have to tape you off and put a sign up.
g_fire_back: Oi, I've carried every one of you out of somewhere this month, butt, so mind your mouth now.
That's lush coming from a man who can't tie a bowline without asking it nicely first.
g_pile_on: Duw, he's right though, I watched him walk into the same branch twice, isn't it, same branch.
And then he tried to blame the map, boys, as if the map had moved the tree.
lines.g_peacemake: Right, enough now, the pair of you, before I pick you both up and put you on different sides of the road.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, butt, I'm with him on this one, and I'd say so to your face in the pub.
lines.g_left_out: No, you carry on, the two of you, I'll go and check the straps on the cart, someone has to.
lines.g_include: Come here, mun, get in by the fire, there's a cuppa with your name on it and I won't take no.
lines.g_bad_plan: Now, hear me out, boys, what if I just run at the door, proper front row, and we find out which of us is harder?
lines.g_plan_yes: Tidy, I'm in, and if it goes wrong at least it'll make a lush story at the bar.
lines.g_plan_no: No chance, butt, I've built enough things to know when one's about to fall over, and that one's leaning already.
lines.g_hype: Right, boys, heads up, bind on, and nobody steps back! We go in like it's the last ten minutes against Cardiff.
lines.g_toast: Glasses up, this lot! To the boys who stand where the weight comes, and to the pint after.
lines.g_cheers: Iechyd da, everyone, and somebody start a song before I do it myself.
g_quiet_line: That strap's going to go, by the way, the brown one, I'll sort it now in a minute.
Well, there we are then, as my mam would say, and put the kettle on.
lines.g_after_wipe: Up you get, boys, slowly now, nobody's broken, I checked. We go again once we've had a cuppa.
lines.g_crew: You're my front row now, the lot of you. I'd stand in front of anything for any of you, and that's not talk.
lines.g_exasperated: Duw, Duw, the state of you! Will one of you please check a knot before you jump off something?
lines.g_love_sharp: You say it straight and quick, butt, like a good ref. No messing, no dressing it up, I love that.
lines.g_love_kind: You look after people without a fuss, butt. My mam's like that, and it's the best thing a person can be.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh till my ribs hurt, and I've had my ribs stood on by Bridgend forwards. That's saying something.
lines.g_love_brave: You go in first like a proper flanker, no thought for yourself, and I'll always be right behind you.
lines.g_love_steady: You don't move, butt, whatever comes at you. That's the best thing I can say about anyone, on a pitch or off it.
lines.g_love_clever: Your head works like a good engineer's, butt, you see how the weight sits in a thing. I could listen to you all night.
lines.g_love_honest: You've never told me a job was fine when it wasn't. In my trade that's what keeps people alive.
lines.g_love_quiet: You don't say much, butt, but when you do it's worth hearing. Like a good tighthead, all work, no noise.
lines.g_love_fierce: Quit isn't in you, mun, not once. You'd have made a lush number seven.
lines.g_love_warm: You make anywhere feel like the clubhouse on a Saturday, butt, and I've missed that more than I'll say.
g_loved: Get away with you, you'll have me welling up, and I'm a big lump to have crying on you.
Duw, now I've got to buy you a pint, that's the rules, I don't make them.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You've always got to have the clever little dig, haven't you? It's not big, butt, it's just small.
lines.g_hate_kind: You fuss over me like I'm made of glass, and I'm the size of a door. Leave off, mun.
lines.g_hate_funny: Not everything's a laugh, butt, some things you take seriously or somebody gets hurt.
lines.g_hate_brave: You run in without looking, every time, and one day I won't be quick enough to stand in front of you.
lines.g_hate_steady: You'd check the same knot ten times, mun, and the job's still not done by teatime.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain it to me like I'm thick, butt. I build things for a living, I know how weight works.
lines.g_hate_honest: You say every last thing you think, the second you think it. Some things want a minute first, mun.
lines.g_hate_quiet: Not a word out of you all day, and I can't tell if you're fine or about to fall off something.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a contest with you, even the walking. It's not a cup final, butt, it's a road.
lines.g_hate_warm: Your mouth hasn't stopped since breakfast, butt, and I've shared a minibus with a whole rugby team.
lines.g_respect: I'm not going to pretend I like you, butt. But you held your ground back there, and I'll shake your hand for that much.
lines.g_call_out: That one's on you, butt, and you know it. You went in before anyone was set and I had to scrape you off the floor.
lines.g_stung: Right, tidy, thank you for that. I'm going to check some knots for a bit, on my own.
lines.g_concede: Fair play, butt, back there, that was me, and I've been chewing it over. Here, I've redone your strap, it was going anyway.
lines.g_nod: Don't go making a speech of it. You did all right yourself, mind, I'll say that much.
lines.g_callback_save: You remember pulling me out of that mine, butt? I'm buying your pints until the day I die for that.
lines.g_callback_clutch: Last two standing, you and me, and you said we should've brought a ball. Best moment I've had in this world.
lines.g_callback_callout: Last time you had a go at me I sulked for a whole day, butt, and you were right, which was worse.
lines.g_former_rivals: When I met you I wanted to put you through a wall, butt, no word of a lie, and now here we are, cwtching.
lines.g_changed: I let the fire come today and I didn't flinch from it, and I didn't enjoy it either. Just held it, steady, like a scrum.
g_unguarded: Come here, all of you, I'll tell you the real reason I sing up the scaffold. It's so my hands don't shake.
My nephews used to stand on my feet and I'd walk them round the kitchen like that. I think about it every morning.
lines.g_clipped: Fine, butt, I'll be checking the cart. Shout if you need lifting.
lines.g_noticed_open: Listen to you, butt, chatting away like a Saturday night! I knew you had it in you, mun.
arg_ask: {player}, you tell him, go on, you've got the sense here and he won't listen to a scaffolder.
Right, {player}, you're the ref, you make the call, and whoever loses buys the first round.
lines.arg_backed_me: There we are, the ref has spoken! Your round then, butt, and get me a big one.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fair enough, ref's decision, I'll take it on the chin. Wrong, mind, but I'll take it.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Useless, {player}, like a ref who's left his whistle in the car.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Every call goes his way, {player}, every one. I'm starting to think you're on his team.
lines.arg_wallflower: No ref, then, so I'm calling it myself. I win, butt, and you're making the tea.
lines.arg_reject: No, with respect, {player}, no. I've been up a pole in a gale, and I know which way this falls.
lines.arg_grumble: Still think I was right about that, butt, I'm only mentioning it the once over my pint.
lines.arg_settled: Ah, come here, we're both half right, isn't it. Shake on it and we'll call it a draw.
lines.seen_listens: You let a man finish his story, {player}. My dad's like that, and it's rarer than you'd think.
lines.seen_truth: No messing with you, {player}, you'd tell me if my ties weren't holding. I trust that.
lines.seen_jokes: Every time it goes wrong you crack a joke, {player}, like a captain in the huddle, and it works.
lines.seen_stays_out: You keep well out of other people's rows, {player}. Wise man, my mam would like you.
lines.seen_biased: There's a teacher's pet in this lot, {player}, and the whole stand can see who it is.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be hard on people, {player}. I'm a big lad, but some of these aren't, mind.
lines.seed_right: {player}, what you told me that day we all got flattened, I didn't like it one bit. Today it kept me on my feet, so ta.
lines.seed_remember: That thing you said to me, after the bad day, it's been going round my head like a hymn I can't finish.
lines.seed_wrong: I tried it your way, {player}, honest, and it went worse. No hard feelings, just letting you know.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Got a minute, {player}? That was close, and I felt the fire come up again, and I wanted it to.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: The whole lot of us flattened, {player}, like a collapsed scrum. I keep counting heads, can't stop myself.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} hit the deck before anyone, and I was stood right next to him, {player}. I'm meant to be the one in front.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: We did it, {player}, the whole thing, start to whistle! I want to sing, honest to God, stop me.
lines.talk_development: Can I ask you something, {player}? The fire, when it comes. Does it look like me doing it, or like something else?
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been hard on {name}, I reckon. He's a different sort of player, that's all, and I wanted him in my position.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Tell me straight, {player}, does {name} want me about, or am I just the big lump who carries things?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} gets right up my nose, butt, no word of a lie. But he's bloody good, and that's what gets me.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: Something's not right with {name}, {player}. Quiet, like a lad who's hiding a bad knee.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: A word, {player}, if you have a minute? Anything worth having goes straight to {name}. I'm not blind, I can count, and I'm tired of counting.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: Cards on the table, {player}. Me and {name} don't get on, never have, and I'm sick of shaking his hand in the tunnel.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: {player}, we keep getting flattened, over and over. I'm all for a hard game, but this is just reckless.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: That thing {name} told me, the other day. He had it right and I had it wrong, and I'm a big enough lump to own that.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Do you trust me, {player}? Because when it counts you leave me on the bench, and I'm built for the front.
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: You took my kit and gave it to {name} without a word, {player}. I'd have handed it over myself, you only had to ask.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Ta, {player}, I needed that. Right, I'll put the kettle on now, and you're having a cup.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: Aye, I know, I know. I'll be right as rain in a bit, I always am.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Right, well, that's not what a man wants with his hands still shaking. I'm going to check some knots.
lines.talk_lands_development: You see it too, then. Tidy, that helps, more than you'd know.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, we'll see. It's a long season, isn't it.
lines.talk_stings_development: No, that's not it, butt. Leave it there for now, I've got straps to check.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Right, I'll go and have a word with {name}, man to man, over a cuppa. Ta for that.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: We'll see, {player}. People take longer than a roof, and a roof takes long enough.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Pretend I never opened my mouth, butt, and not a word to {name}, right?
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Fair enough, that's fair, {player}. Still a bit sore, mind, but it'll pass by tea.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Heard you, {player}. I'll think on it up the next scaffold.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: That's how it is, then? Right, at least I know where I'm stood now.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, we're done with this, butt. I'll be at the cart if you want anything lifted.
lines.arc_cracks: That last fight, boys, the fire came up and I let it, and I'm not sorry. Is that bad? Because it felt lush, boys, and that's the truth of it.
lines.arc_turn: The night the naga came, I burned one where it stood, in front of half the town, and it felt like the best tackle of my life. That's what frightens me, boys.
lines.arc_become: I've got hold of it now, the fire, like a scrum I'm anchoring. Steady and on purpose. It's mine, and it's not the real me, the singing is.
lines.arc_failed: Don't look at me like that, boys. The fire's what I am now, and it's about time I stopped apologising for it.
lines.alt_turn: There was a lad on my scaffold the night the naga came, boys. They pulled him off it, and he broke his leg, and I carried him in. I built that scaffold.
lines.alt_become: I went and saw that ranger, the one who fell. Told him I was sorry, and he laughed at me, said he'd do it again. I think I can let it go now.
g_roast_after: Look at you lot, the worst front row in Azeroth, and I wouldn't swap one of you for the Lions.
You're a shambles, boys, an absolute shambles, and you're my shambles, so mind it.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Up, boys, nice and slow, I've got you. Fire's quiet in me tonight, and that's how I like it.
lines.g_toast_after: To my mam, who always said I sang because I was happy. She was half right, and tonight she's all right.
lines.g_crew_after: You're my front row, boys, and I'll hold for you, steady, no fire unless you need it.
g_quiet_line_after: Hands are steady tonight, butt, look. Thought you'd want to know.
There's a hymn I couldn't remember the end of for two years, and it came back this morning.
g_loved_after: Ta, butt, I'll keep that one, no joke about it.
Come here, mun, get in for a cwtch, I'm not letting that pass without one.

history.open: Fifteen years in the front row for Pontypridd, {player}, every Saturday, rain or worse. Ask me anything about rugby, go on.

options.text: What's the front row actually for?
options.reply: Standing where the weight comes and not moving, butt. Everyone else gets the glory, we get the cauliflower ears and the pint after. Best job in the world.

options.text: Isn't it just a game for thugs?
options.reply: Oi, oi, I'll forgive you that once, because you've never been in a scrum. It's the most honest game there is, mun, nobody can hide.
The pint after, honest to God. The singing, the lads, the bus home. Not even the game. Saturday, all of it.

history.open: Nobody's ever fallen off anything I built, {player}. Not once, in twenty years of scaffolding. That's the one thing I'm proud of.

options.text: That's something to be proud of.
options.reply: It is, isn't it. You check every tie, every board, every knot, and you never get bored of checking. That's the whole trick.

options.text: Not once? That's a big claim.
options.reply: Not once on Earth, butt. Here's a different story, and I'm not ready to tell it yet. Now in a minute, maybe.

options.text: Is that why you check everyone's straps?
options.reply: Aye, caught me. Can't help it, mun. If it's hanging loose, my hands go to it before my head's decided.

history.open: My sister Carys has two boys, {player}. I used to take them to the match and buy them chips and get told off for it after.

options.reply: Rhys and Owen, eight and six when I last saw them. Proper little terrors, the pair. Rhys wanted to be a hooker, like his uncle, and I nearly cried.

options.text: You'd have been a good dad.
options.reply: Duw, maybe, I don't know. I liked being the uncle, isn't it. All the fun and you hand them back sticky.
Maybe, butt, maybe. I don't say it out loud much in case it hears me. But I'm keeping a chips budget, just in case.

friend.open: You're one of my boys now, {player}, my front row. That means I'll stand in front of anything for you, no questions.

options.text: Then I'll be right behind you.
options.reply: That's the way, butt. You push, I hold, and nothing gets through us.

options.text: Do I have to learn the songs?
options.reply: Every word, mun, and I'll be testing you in the next tavern.

sworn.open: Here, take this. My podger spanner, from the scaffolds at home. Had it on my wrist the day I came through. I want you to have it.

options.reply: You can, and you will, butt. I've got the fire now, I don't need the spanner to hold things together any more.
I know you will. Check your straps with it, now and then, for me.

reconciled.open: Me and {name} had it out, {player}, properly, over a cuppa. I think we're sorted now, and I wanted you to know first.

options.reply: Too short for grudges, aye. Long enough for tea, though.
Nothing much, butt. We both said sorry at the same time and then laughed like idiots.
